bookTitle: Wally the Whale and the Great Harbor
bigIdea: Put your stuff in a crate with everything it needs, and it works on every island.

characters.name: Wally
characters.want: deliver every friend's cargo to every island exactly as packed, with no surprises
characters.visual: chubby friendly whale in side view, smooth rounded body, five simple curved belly stripes, one big round eye, small flat captain's cap on top of head, no arms, small fins
characters.realMapsTo: the Docker daemon/server (does the heavy work)

characters.name: Pip
characters.visual: small sea otter standing upright, round head, two small round ears, short whiskers, striped scarf, two paws held in front of chest, short tail

characters.name: Skipper
characters.visual: round seagull standing on a wooden post, open pointed beak, small sailor hat, two thin legs, wings folded at sides, megaphone on a stand beside him

setting: a busy island harbor with docks, a packing shed, a lighthouse, a library, open sea lanes, and a village

conceptLadder.title: The Island Mix-Up
conceptLadder.idea: A container wraps one app with everything it needs, so it runs the same anywhere.
conceptLadder.mechanism: Pack code plus its exact tools into a sealed standard box. The box runs identically on any machine. The old way (virtual machine) builds a whole computer per app, which is heavy and slow.
conceptLadder.metaphor: a sealed sea-chest; old way = a whole little ship per parcel
conceptLadder.simplificationHides: crates share the host's engine (corrected in S16)
conceptLadder.failureCase: Pip's cake works at home but arrives flat on the island

conceptLadder.title: Skipper's Shouting Post
conceptLadder.idea: Docker is two parts: the client gives orders, the server (daemon) does the work, talking over an agreed API.
conceptLadder.mechanism: The client sends commands. The daemon receives them and does the heavy work (building, running, stopping). They communicate via API, so the client can be on a different machine.
conceptLadder.metaphor: megaphone and signal flags; Skipper shouts, Wally works
conceptLadder.failureCase: Skipper shouts but nobody answers; he's pointing at the wrong bay

conceptLadder.title: Wally's Floating Tank
conceptLadder.idea: On Mac and Windows, the Docker server needs a hidden Linux VM to live in.
conceptLadder.mechanism: Docker's server is a Linux program. On Mac/Windows it runs inside a small Linux virtual machine. Install both halves, then test with a tiny hello-world container.
conceptLadder.metaphor: a floating water tank giving Wally water on a dry shore
conceptLadder.failureCase: Skipper shouts and Wally can't move on dry land

arc.act1: S1-S3: Wally learns the crate idea, meets Skipper, gets set up
arc.act2: S4-S12: building well and keeping crates running well
arc.act3: S13-S18: one crate becomes a fleet, then a self-healing system

runningGags: The hello-world crate from S3 appears in every later chapter, getting more decorated
Skipper shouts orders through a megaphone; by S15 he uses flags, in S18 he just nods
The island on the horizon gains a light each time a delivery goes right
